26#main: A slave acquires himself with money, principal limbs, or document. How with money? One gave the master money and said on condition your slave goes out with them to freedom — once the master accepted money or money's worth, the slave goes out free without the slave's intent; and if another gave the slave money on condition you go out with them to freedom — if the master wishes to accept the money, the slave goes free; if not, the slave did not acquire the money (Rambam chapter 5 of Laws of Slaves halacha 2): {Rama: (And some say he can also acquire himself by chalipin if he has an item for chalipin, such as given to go out with it to freedom) (Tur in the name of Rabbenu Tam, Raavad in hasagot, Rabbeinu Yerucham).}
27#main: How with principal limbs? A slave circumcised and immersed for servitude — if his master blinded his eye, knocked out his tooth, or cut off one of the tips of fingers of hands and feet, ear tips, nose tip, reproductive tip, or woman's breast tips — he goes out to freedom and needs a bill of release: {Rama: (And they compel the master to write him a bill of release) (Beit Yosef in the name of Rabbeinu Yerucham).} But if his tongue was cut — he does not go out to freedom.
28#main: If his testicles were crushed and healed completely from the pouch — he goes out to freedom; but if cut and still hanging in the pouch — he does not go out to freedom.
29#main: If he had an extra finger and cut it — if it stands in the row of fingers, he goes out to freedom.
30#main: If he plucked his beard and a bone fell from the jaw — he goes out to freedom.
31#main: If struck his hand and it withered and will return — he does not go out to freedom.
32#main: Knocked out a minor's tooth that will be replaced — he does not go out to freedom.
33#main: If his eye was somewhat dim and struck it and blinded — if initially usable somewhat, he goes out for it to freedom; but if gouged even if never usable at all, he goes out to freedom for a limb was lacking; and the same for a limb that was idle and not used for work — if cut, he goes out for a limb was lacking.
34#main: Struck his eye and lessened its light, on his tooth and loosened — if still usable, he does not go out to freedom.
35#main: Struck his eye and blinded, his ear and deafened — he goes out to freedom; but if struck the wall opposite his eye or ear and he was startled until he does not see or hear — he does not go out to freedom.
36#main: In all these he does not go out to freedom until the master acts intentionally; therefore if intended to throw a stone at an animal and it fell on the slave and cut his finger or knocked out his tooth — he does not go out; and if he reached into his maidservant's womb and blinded a fetus in her womb — he does not go out, for he did not know he would intend that; but if his master was a doctor and said treat my eye and he blinded — he goes out, for he intended to destroy.
37#main: One who is half slave half free, or a slave of two partners — they do not go out through principal limbs, for the verse says "his slave" dedicated to him.
38#main: Iron-flock slaves (dowry property the wife brings and husband accepts liability even if lost) — go out through principal limbs for a man but not a woman; melog property slaves do not go out for man or woman.
39#main: Knocked out his slave's tooth and blinded his eye — he goes out with the tooth and does not pay eye value; if he seized, they do not remove from his hand; and if he wrote a bill of release between knocking tooth and blinding eye, he must pay eye value.
40#main: A slave's release through principal limbs — even though it is a fine — applies in the present time; if witnesses come on the matter, he cannot use him; and some wrote they excommunicate him until he writes a bill of release: {Rama: (And likewise if the master admitted himself) (Tur in the name of Rambam and Rosh).}
41#main: How with a document? He writes on paper or pottery, behold you are free, or behold you are your own, or I have no business with you, and gives to his hand or another on his behalf — even without the slave's knowledge, for it is a merit that he leave his master's hand to freedom; and if he protests at receiving, he does not go out to freedom with it.
42#main: If he said one of these formulas orally — it is nothing.
43#main: One who writes to his maidservant, behold you are permitted to any man — this is not language of release.
44#main: If he gave the document before witnesses, or witnesses signed and gave it between themselves — he goes out to freedom; and some say it must be given before witnesses; and if we see it signed, we need not bring witnesses of delivery, for we assume it was duly delivered.
45#main: In six matters release of slaves equals women's gittin; in other matters they are like other documents; these six: invalid in gentile courts, valid with Samaritan witness; require writing for the freed one himself; not written on connected sheets; sign only one before the other — both gittin and release documents are equal in bringing and delivering.
46#main: How so? All documents that rise in gentile courts are valid under conditions explained in laws of loans, except women's gittin and slave release documents.
47#main: Any document with even one Samaritan witness is invalid, except women's gittin and slave release — valid with one Israelite and one Samaritan witness, provided the Samaritan is a companion; and in the present time when Samaritans are like gentiles for all their matters, we learn from them regarding Sadducees, for Sadducees now are like Samaritans then before they decreed they be like gentiles.
48#main: In a woman's get it says and he wrote for her by name; in a release document it says or she was freed — not given to her until written for her name.
49#main: In a woman's get it says and he wrote and gave — one lacking only delivery goes out; written connected then cut is lacking cutting and delivery; in release it says given to her — lacking only delivery.
50#main: Both women's gittin and slave release documents — they sign only one before the other.
